shared_elements: upright monolithic stele/pillar carved in relief
horizontal band or register dividing the composition
repeated row of small motifs across the upper zone
stacked registers of imagery on a vertical field
justification: Both are upright relief-carved standing stones whose imagery is organised into stacked horizontal registers, with a row of repeated small motifs across an upper band and animal/figural forms below, and both carry a dominant frontal anthropomorphic presence on the shaft. Beyond that generic scheme the content differs sharply: A shows a densely ornamented frontal human figure in elaborate headdress and beaded costume with dense scroll and glyph-like filler covering every surface, while B shows sparse, isolated low-relief animals (a quadruped, birds, a long-necked creature) on a plain ground with an abstract T-shaped pillar body, so the depiction conventions and specific motifs share nothing distinctive.
